decisions.reason: As a camera closely aligned with our long-standing optical navigation business and still given a dedicated product page through 2024, it fits knowledge we already possess and remains commercially improvable.
This modular camera line is core to our established capabilities and its visible ESA HERA mission success strongly supports continued market commitment and further learning across models.
The sensor suite builds directly on our existing space sensing competences and its continued standalone presentation suggests enough strategic value for us to refine it rather than withdraw it.

Although the LiDAR sensor has only limited website prominence, miniaturized space-qualified sensing is close to our technological base and our R&D capacity gives us scope to improve it instead of exiting quickly.
A radiation-hard camera line matches our heritage in reliable space imaging and, as a new multi-model family launched in 2024, is more likely to be developed further than removed.

This asteroid navigation and imaging camera is more niche and only briefly presented so far, but it still builds on our proven mission-camera know-how and benefits from our strong ability to learn from early deployments.
